hypotheses.justification: Removing `ha` leaves the statement `{ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] {τ : ℂ} {a : ι → ℂ} {z : ℂ} (hτ : ‖τ‖ < 1) (hz : z ≠ 0) : DifferentiableAt ℂ (markedThetaProduct τ a) z`, which is still true. By `markedThetaProduct`'s definition the function is the finite product `fun w ↦ ∏ i, thetaProduct τ (w / a i)`, so by `DifferentiableAt.fun_finsetProd` (Mathlib/Analysis/Calculus/Deriv/Mul.lean:447) it suffices to prove each factor differentiable at `z`. Fix `i` and case on `a i = 0`: if `a i ≠ 0`, use `thetaProduct_scaled_differentiableAt hτ h hz`; if `a i = 0`, then by the junk convention `div_zero : c / 0 = 0` (Mathlib/Algebra/GroupWithZero/Basic.lean:401, a `simp` lemma for `GroupWithZero`, and `ℂ` is a field) the factor is the constant function `fun _ ↦ thetaProduct τ 0`, hence differentiable by `differentiableAt_const`. The empty index type is also fine (`Finset.univ.prod` of the empty family is the constant `1`). No degenerate case breaks this: the factor with `a i = 0` is constant in `z`, so the non-junk case `z = 0` is irrelevant there. Note the other hypotheses are genuinely used and cannot be dropped by the same argument: `hz` is needed because for `a i ≠ 0` the second product `thetaPositive τ (τ * a i / z)` has an essential singularity at `z = 0`, and `hτ` enters through `thetaProduct_differentiableAt`; `[Fintype ι]` is needed for the finite product. Incidentally, the `ha`-free version can be proved without changing the conclusion, so `ha` can be deleted independently of the rest.
